experiments.title: Pinned source tensor range census and FP16 decode audit
experiments.hypothesis: The historical W2 non-finite could be caused by source BF16-to-FP16 weight overflow.
experiments.inputs: official HTTPS byte range [11584667040,11946487712) containing the 13 BF16 tensors
experiments.numerical_policy: BF16 bits to exact Float32 semantic value, then IEEE FP16 nearest-even; no clamp or saturation
experiments.expected_observation: either source overflow explains W2 or the causal search moves to the activation path
experiments.actual_observation: all source values were finite; every tensor had zero FP16 overflow and zero saturation. W2 absmax was 1.796875. The census revealed a decoder bug that inflated normal FP16 values by 32768 in the diagnostic executor.
experiments.conclusion: Source-weight conversion overflow is rejected. The historical diagnostic W2 non-finite is confounded by a deterministic FP16 decoder defect and must be re-run with captured inputs before a storage policy is accepted.
experiments.confidence: high for source-weight ranges and decoder causality; no claim yet about correct-path activation ranges
experiments.next_question: With the pinned input and timestep, what is the first non-finite under corrected decode for BF16, FP16, and mixed policies?

experiments.title: Corrected full-path pre-attention and FFN witness replay
experiments.hypothesis: Corrected FP16 decode removes the diagnostic W2 failure, or localizes a distinct activation-path cause.
experiments.inputs: validated local OCT_EVT2_CACHE root containing layers and OCT_EVT2_ORACLE pinned revision root; captured run_02 input and timestep
experiments.numerical_policy: cached FP16 values expanded to FP32; fixed-order FP32 reductions; corrected IEEE binary16 normal exponent decode
experiments.implementation_identity: corrected canonical reference plus Oct witness orchestration
experiments.expected_observation: exact first non-finite or finite canonical stages under each policy
experiments.actual_observation: input, timestep, and cache aggregate validated. Both full diagnostic replays produced final SHA-256 4aff8bf19cfbfc9aebf2e8aa78ef91fb7bb5c117f98504080ed1bc3b206e0c43. W2 and final output are finite; the historical W2 non-finite disappears under corrected normal FP16 decode.
experiments.conclusion: The historical all-FP16 rejection is withdrawn as an inference from the defective diagnostic. It is not an accepted production policy pending Oct-led policy comparisons.
experiments.confidence: high for decoder root cause and replay determinism; medium for one full diagnostic policy
experiments.next_question: O3: generate canonical Oct pre-attention / AdaLN / RMSNorm witnesses and compare source BF16 versus cached FP16 at those boundaries
